name: Tartan
overview: Tartan was a male messenger serving under King Sennacherib, sent to King Hezekiah of Judah as recorded in 2 Kings 18:17. His role was significant as a representative of Assyrian authority during a critical confrontation. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are provided in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Tartan' is a proper name meaning 'supreme commander' or 'second in command,' indicating a high-ranking military position. This title reflects his authoritative role within the Assyrian army, as noted in 2 Kings 18:17.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Tartan beyond his role as a messenger from Sennacherib to Hezekiah. There are no additional relational details provided.
scriptureSignificance: Tartan's significance lies in his function as an envoy of Assyrian power during the reign of Hezekiah, embodying the threat posed by Sennacherib's campaign against Judah. His presence in the biblical narrative highlights the tension between Assyria and Judah and sets the stage for God’s deliverance of His people. Through Tartan, the narrative emphasizes the sovereignty of God over earthly powers and the importance of trusting Him amid political and military threats.
